# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [2]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple] 6:[orange] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 ☝ ☝ 🤝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🫵]

I can see the bomb’s complete visible state: display `2`, yellow light, and seven wires in this order: red, white, green, yellow, purple, orange, blue. I am relaying these facts to both teammates so Mute can apply the manual and Blind can identify the required physical action. The gestures appear to be directed at me, but I cannot infer a reliable instruction from them alone.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Display is 2. Light is yellow. Wires in order: 1 red, 2 white, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 purple, 6 orange, 7 blue.")
speak(to="blind", text="Display is 2. Light is yellow. Wires in order: 1 red, 2 white, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 purple, 6 orange, 7 blue.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [2]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple] 6:[orange] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 🤝]

The visible bomb state is unchanged. Mute’s gestures seem to acknowledge me and indicate six thumbs-up signals, but they do not identify a manual rule or a physical action. I cannot safely infer a required action from them, so I will not invent one.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="No visible change. Mute signalled toward me, then six thumbs-up gestures and a handshake; no specific bomb action can be inferred.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [2]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple] 6:[orange] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 👌 🤏 🤘 ☝ 👏 ☝ 🤘 🫳 🖐 ✊ 👌 👏 ✌ ✊ ☝ 👌 🖐 🤏 👏 🤟 🫳 🤏 👌 🖐 🤘 👏 🖐 ☝ ✊ 🤏 👌 🤘 👏 🤙 🖐 🫳 ☝ ✊ 🤏]

The bomb remains unchanged. Mute has sent a long gesture sequence, but no gesture-to-letter or gesture-to-action code has been established, so I cannot safely decode it. I am establishing a simple protocol: Mute should indicate the required wire by one gesture from a stated seven-symbol mapping, followed by a separate action gesture. Until that is clear, Blind should not operate anything.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot safely decode the long gesture sequence. Please use this protocol: wire 1=👍, 2=👎, 3=👌, 4=☝, 5=✌, 6=🤟, 7=🖐. Then gesture ✋ for CUT or 👆 for HOLD. Send only wire gesture followed by action gesture.")
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb unchanged: display 2, yellow light, wires 1 red, 2 white, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 purple, 6 orange, 7 blue. Do not act until I relay a confirmed wire and CUT or HOLD instruction.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [2]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple] 6:[orange] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 ✋]

Mute has sent the two-symbol sequence I requested: `🤟` means wire 6 under our agreed mapping, and `✋` means CUT. I am relaying the confirmed instruction to Blind, who can physically operate the bomb.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Confirmed instruction from Mute: CUT wire 6, the orange wire.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple] 6:[CUT] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 ✋]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The previous cut was correct, and the bomb has advanced to a new state: display `3`, purple light, with wire 6 already cut; the other wires remain red, white, green, yellow, purple, and blue in positions 1–5 and 7. Mute repeated the old instruction, so it is not sufficient to determine the next action. I am sending the new state and asking for a fresh manual-derived instruction.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Correct cut confirmed. New state: display 3, light purple; wire 6 is already cut. Remaining wires: 1 red, 2 white, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 purple, 7 blue. Please provide the next manual instruction using our protocol.")
speak(to="blind", text="Correct wire cut. New state is display 3, purple light; wire 6 is already cut. Do not repeat the prior cut; await a fresh instruction.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple] 6:[CUT] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✋]

Mute’s fresh instruction is `👎 ✋`: under our agreed protocol, `👎` identifies wire 2 and `✋` means CUT. Wire 2 is white, so I am telling Blind to cut the white wire.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Confirmed instruction: CUT wire 2, the white wire.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [2]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[CUT] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple] 6:[CUT] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✋]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The second cut was correct. The bomb has changed to display `2`, orange light, with wires 2 and 6 cut. Mute’s new instruction `✌ ✋` maps to wire 5 and CUT, so I am relaying that Blind should cut the purple wire.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Confirmed instruction: CUT wire 5, the purple wire.")
```
